What's next for Curry and the Warriors?
Stephen Curry's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings.

The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer.

By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million.

For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer.

Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski. The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks

Grading the Curry deal: Why Warriors don't get an A

Hornets star Knueppel sidelined by hamstring injury
The Charlotte Hornets announced that Kon Knueppel will be out for at least the entire preseason because of a left hamstring injury.

James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers
LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July.

"[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump."

Grizzlies waive Russell
The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

stories.headline: Lone'er Kavanagh: Win in 'dangerous' UFC 333 fight puts me in title contention
stories.summary: Brit Lone'er Kavanagh believes victory against Ramazonbek Temirov at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi could catapult him into flyweight title contention.
stories.body:
Brit Lone'er Kavanagh believes victory against Ramazonbek Temirov at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi could catapult him into flyweight title contention.

Kavanagh (10-2) is coming off a fight of the night defeat to Brandon Royval in July, a result that followed his breakout win over former champion Brandon Moreno in Mexico City earlier this year.

Uzbekistan's Temirov (20-3) is yet to taste defeat in the UFC octagon and is on a 12-fight win streak.

Kavanagh has said that a positive result in the Middle East could reignite his momentum in the featherweight division after the submission defeat to Royval last time out.

"I believe so. I'd like to think [it puts me into the featherweight title mix]," Kavanagh told ESPN.

"I think a win there puts me right back up there. He's a dangerous opponent. He's got some good wins under him, a lot of wins, but I think a win against him puts me right back up at the top. [I'm] always looking for a finish.

"He's dangerous. He throws big shots, he throws wild shots. He's constantly [moving] forwards. He likes to stand and bang. Those are the main things I think that stick out. Obviously he's got a good wrestling background as well.

"His main weapons are his heavy hands, and that excites me. I love fights like that and I think it's a good fight for me.

"Hopefully [another fight of the night], I'm looking for more performances of the night. Kavanagh was unranked before his decision win against Moreno and will now be a part of his second numbered UFC card, with his last fight at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas on the night of Conor McGregor's ill-fated return against Max Holloway.

"It feels surreal, I'm very grateful I get these opportunities, being on a card with such big names, being high up, it's amazing. I'm very blessed," he said.

"If you told me 10 years ago I'd be fighting on cards like these, I'd have told you to do one, so it's very cool.

"It was an awesome opportunity to fight on that card, McGregor coming back, in Vegas, such a high-level fight. I'd like to think my style is entertaining as it is, I'm always looking to be in an entertaining fight and apart from that I just love fighting so just being in there is cool.

"I've gone from watching [UFC YouTube show] Embedded to actually being in it so that was cool!"

stories.headline: Tasmania Devils unveil top teenagers as first signings
stories.summary: Eight teenagers, including a highly fancied Western Australian youngster, have become the Tasmania Devils' maiden AFL signings.
stories.body:
Highly touted Western Australian youngster Axel Walsh, a host of Victorians and one local talent have been snapped up by the Tasmania Devils as their first signings.

The club, which will enter the AFL and AFLW in 2028, on Tuesday night revealed eight under-17 players it had signed as part of its list-concession build.

Tasmania can sign up to 12 pre-draft 17-year-old players across 2026 and 2027, taking them out of the AFL draft.

Top of the tree was Walsh, an athletic 202cm forward-ruck who averaged 12.8 disposals and 10.3 hitouts and kicked three goals in four matches at the most recent under-18 carnival.

He was likely to be the No.1 pick in the 2027 draft.

Victorians Jake Miller, Angus Brown, Riley Stratford, Baxter Sruk, Griffin Barker and Nate Jenkins have also joined.

Miller, at 197cm, has been described as a regular goal kicker at club and school level, Brown has a zippy running game, while midfielder Sruk has an ability to rack up possessions.

Tasmanian draft prospect Hugh McCallum, who was sidelined this season with a knee injury, has also been signed.

A lightly-framed wingman or half-forward, McCallum is the brother of former Port Adelaide-listed defender Tom McCallum.

The Devils will be hoping the group can follow the lead of Jeremy Cameron, Dylan Shiel and Adam Treloar, who forged successful careers after being signed by the Giants through the same concession rules prior to their inaugural 2012 season.

"It's a proud moment to welcome our first group of Tasmania Devils players to our state," coach Ken Hinkley said in a club statement.

"I am excited to be working with such a talented group of young footballers, all of whom have tremendous skill sets and AFL attributes already."

McCallum was the final player announced - etching his name in history as the first native Devils contracted player.

"I'm stoked to be a part of it. Growing up you used to have to go to the mainland to play AFL," he said.

Players were assessed at national championships, school and local matches, and were benchmarked against their age group.

All pre-listed players will move to the state in November and begin their preparation for 2028 with individualised training programs.

The under-17 concessions are among the generous list-build options available to the Devils, who also have seven first-round draft picks in 2027 including the first and the third.

stories.headline: Soccer's best 2025-26 kits: The most stylish jerseys you probably missed
stories.summary: While the world's top clubs release their new kits on a wave of hype, there are many more who release absolutely banging jerseys that deserve to be seen.
stories.body:
While the likes of Barcelona, Real Madrid, Paris Saint-Germain and all of the Premier League big hitters have their new kits released on a wave of hype, they make up just a small percentage of the soccer jerseys on sale each season.

For every European heavyweight's flashy, expensive launch campaign, there are hundreds of smaller clubs world who have put just as much effort and ingenuity into their new kit concepts and designs for a much smaller audience.

So after casting a discerning eye over the various home, away and third shirts released for the 2026-27 season, we feel it our sworn duty to help showcase some of the finest, most brilliant and super-stylish concepts that have been rolled out by clubs at all levels of the game over the past couple of months.

- Soccer's wildest warmup kits: The good, the bad and the ugly

- A kit fit for the GOAT: Messi's special kit for Argentina farewell

- Premier League 2026-27 kits: Ranking every jersey released

Here, in alphabetical order, is our considered pick of some of the best football kits that you might not have had the pleasure of seeing until now.

Ajax away (Adidas)

Dutch giants Ajax have added yet another beauty to their ever-increasing catalogue of handsome alternative kits. Predominantly black and burnished gold, this shirt also features an elaborate light grey graphic incorporating outlined images of nine of the club's most significant historic achievements; from their four European Cup/UEFA Champions League titles to winning their 30th Eredivisie shield in 2011.

Angers away (Nike)

Exquisite silver-on-silver design from the Ligue 1 side who have used a cool, retro Total 90 template to create a rather special away kit akin to a suit of gleaming futuristic titanium armor.

Atalanta away (New Balance)

This season sees the return of a classic for Atalanta, who have successfully resurrected their glorious white away kit of the late 1980s and early '90s. The modern incarnation retains the zigzag graphic of the original, but reapplies it across the chest with a touch of added contemporary panache.

Celta Vigo third (Hummel)

Celta have traipsed back through their archives in search of inspiration and settled on a gorgeous red diamond pattern inspired by their cult classic 1995-96 "harlequin print" away kit. While still positively oozing with retro appeal, the modern take is even sweeter.

Como home (Adidas)

Como are very much the new kids on the block in the Serie A style stakes, and this season they will be bringing their elegant aesthetic to the Champions League. In essence, the home jersey is a classic polo-style design in blue which mirrors the color of the water of the famous Lake Como. The lines are incredibly clean and the red, white and gold tricolore trim ices the cake perfectly.

FC Basel third (Macron)

Basel seem to swing wildly between the sublime and the ridiculous when it comes to kit designs, but thankfully the Swiss club's 2026-27 third kit is firmly in the former category. The navy ensemble is an amalgam of several of their historic uniforms with the large fold-over collar, subtle pinstriping and delicate jacquard textures all combining to create a refined aesthetic. However, the real star of the show is that ultra cool "whiteout" FCB crest.

Flamengo third (Adidas)

Harking all the way back to Flamengo's original formation as a Rio de Janeiro rowing club in the late 19th Century, the Brazilian side's new third kit is awash with maritime references, most notably the special "oars and anchor" rowing crest that adorns the chest. That same emblem can also be found repeated in the wave pattern that ripples across the entire shirt.

Genoa away (Kappa)

Another kit drawing inspiration from the 19th century, Genoa's pristine new away kit is a love letter to their beginnings as a football and cricket club in 1893. Italy's oldest existing football team have marked that fact with a light cream jersey that resembles the uniforms initially worn by their players before they first adopted their now-familiar Rossoblù (red and blue) half-and-half shirts in 1901. Those colors are referenced in the club crest, kit sponsor logo and sleeve cuffs in a wonderful bit of detailing.

Grimsby Town away (Lotto)

In what might just be the most brazen "homage" of all time, Grimsby have lifted their new away kit directly from mid-'90s AC Milan, replicating the Rossoneri's all-time classic blue-grey and red geometric design in an almost perfect shot-for-shot recreation. Thankfully, Lotto were also responsible for producing those iconic Milan jerseys back in the day, so the Mariners are unlikely to fall foul of any potential plagiarism issues.

Leicester City away (Adidas)

It might coincide with the former Premier League champions' relegation down to the third tier of English football, but the Foxes will at least look glorious on the road in League One this season. Their away kit is inspired by medieval King Richard III (whose remains were famously found beneath a carpark in the city) and comes with royal burgundy flocking and the same lovely retro fox crest worn by the club during the 1980s.

Lyon third (Adidas)

A strong contender for the grooviest football shirt released this season, Lyon paid tribute to their home city's reputation as the hotbed of the French funk music scene by plying their third shirt with psychedelic waves and trippy trim. There is also a repeating circular graphic embossed within the fabric that resembles vinyl records, just to really cement the funky aesthetic.

Monaco third (Mizuno)

Mizuno have made some delightful kits for Monaco in recent years, and the 2026-27 third shirt is no exception. The base color is white, which is then overlaid with a sumptuous minty green graphic that is intended to reflect the sparkling turquoise waters of the natural pools that speckle the picturesque Monegasque coast. It almost brings vibes of a long, hot summer spent idling on the French Riviera.

Os Belenenses home (Hummel)

One of the oldest sporting clubs in Portugal, Belenenses have gone all the way back to the beginning and drummed up a delightful retro home kit. As well as featuring their classic royal blue club colors and red cross crest, it also carries a mosaic graphic pattern made up of miniature tiles detailing individual elements of their own history and local culture, architecture and identity -- from sailing ships to cathedrals.

Sheffield Wednesday away (Umbro)

It's tough to pick a winner between Sheffield Wednesday's new retro home and away kits, but we think the lean and lovely yellow and black away jersey just about pips it. Umbro have reprised and modernized their designs from the 1992-93 season, which were the last they provided for the Owls before Puma stepped in for the decade that followed.

Strasbourg away (Adidas)

Another strong contender for kit of the year, Strasbourg's away shirt is once again a deliberate recreation of a retro classic. Nostalgia aside, the reworking is a vast improvement on the 1994-96 original, with extra light blue hues helping to create a more delicate diamond pattern which works wonderfully well to frame the oval-shaped heritage RCS crest, which was first worn by the club between 1920 and 1945.

SV Wehen Wiesbaden away (Errea)

German third-tier outfit Wiesbaden are punching well above their weight here. Their away kit is adorned with the famed art nouveau stylings of their home city, which boasts a plethora of ornately decorated buildings, municipal halls, galleries and museums. The result is a lush, verdant green jersey which is festooned with ornate floral motifs and highlighted with lovely bronze flecks here and there.

TSV Eintracht Braunschweig third (Umbro)

Using the slate grey shield of the Braunschweig coat of arms as a jumping-off point, the German second-tier side have concocted a smart kit that looks like it has been plucked straight out of the 1980s. The tonal muted greys are nicely balanced and allow the pops of color on the crest and trim to stand out.

Venezia home (Nocta)

One of an increasing number of clubs who have turned to fashion and streetwear labels to help create their kits, this season's offerings from Venezia are the third produced by Nike's Drake-affiliated brand Nocta. They might also be the best yet, with the diagonally split orange and green bar across the midriff of the home shirt providing a particularly cool "billboard" for the sponsor logo.

VfB Stuttgart away, Europe (Jako)

To coincide with their return to the Champions League, Stuttgart have revived one of the most symbolic kits to feature in their European history. Indeed, the red shirt worn during a UEFA Cup first-round game against Banyasz Tatabanya back in 1988 is an artefact of Europe's history, in a way.

Several hundred intrepid Stuttgart fans made the trip from the former West Germany behind the Iron Curtain to Hungary to watch their side lose 2-1 on the night, only to advance to the second round on aggregate.

The German club decided to reward their raucous travelling support by doling out all of the players' match-worn kit among the away section after the final whistle. Stuttgart then battled to the 1988-89 UEFA Cup final, only to narrowly lose out against Diego Maradona's Napoli over two legs.

After being given away to fans, the "Tatabanya" kit was never worn again -- but almost 40 years later, the same red lozenge pattern has been resurrected to help instill the same resilience on Stuttgart's latest continental quest. A mini-history lesson, and also a work of true retro brilliance.

stories.headline: Five stats: Why USMNT should be excited about Cavan Sullivan
stories.summary: Is the hype around Cavan Sullivan's USMNT future too much? No, it's actually not enough -- and here are five reasons why.
stories.body:
There's something incredible happening in MLS right now, and the average World Cup watcher probably has no clue.

Seriously, think about all of the people you know who are "sports fans" but maybe not "soccer fans" -- the ones who root hard for the U.S. men's national team every four years and know the names of their four or five best players.

Sure, they probably still can't pronounce the last name of manager Mauricio Pochettino, but they watched tons of soccer this summer. The World Cup had so many games, and finally, it was all aligned with our time zones. These people now have opinions about VAR, England's prevent defense and the general moral fiber of the Argentina national team.

They're primed to care about soccer, especially American soccer, and especially a kind of greatness we've never seen before from a player of a certain age. No, I'm not talking about Lionel Messi, who somehow (1) might still be the greatest soccer player in the world, (2) is easily the greatest 39-year-old soccer player we've ever seen, and (3) continues to play soccer every week, across North America, without having any effect on North American sports discourse.

No, I'm talking about Cavan Sullivan, the 16-year-old phenom who, somehow, still feels as if he's being underhyped.

The history of American soccer is filled with players who were overpromised and couldn't do anything but underdeliver, but this is different. It's not just that we, Americans, have never seen someone like Sullivan. No, the wider soccer world -- the rest of the entire world -- rarely ever sees someone like Sullivan.

Here are some numbers for why you should get excited:

1,675 minutes
As I like to often say: The best predictor of future stardom is minutes players at a young age.

Take the three front-runners for this year's Ballon d'Or. Harry Kane was playing and scoring goals for Millwall in the Championship during his age-18 season. Lamine Yamal is 19 -- right now. And Kylian Mbappé broke out for Monaco during his age-17 season.

Sullivan is currently in his age-16 season (defined by your age at the start of the campaign). And so far, he has played 1,675 league minutes in MLS.

The site FBref has data for what they call the "Next 14" -- essentially, the most competitive leagues in the world after Europe's Big Five -- that goes back to the beginning of the current century, if not more. Only 21 outfield players have played more league minutes than Sullivan, who still has at least eight games left in his season. If we expand the dataset to include the Big Five, then only five other players -- Eduardo Camavinga, Alex Song, Gavi, Lamine Yamal, and Nuri Sahin -- have played more minutes than Sullivan before their age-17 season.

The leader, among all of these players? Freddy Adu had played 5,448 minutes by the end of his age-16 season.

€1.54 billion
Though we don't have much useful leaguewide data dating to 2006, when Adu was wrapping up his age-16 season, I do feel confident in saying the following: MLS is a lot better than it was 20 years ago.

Heck, it's a lot better than it was even 10 years ago. Per a recent analysis by Michael Caley: In 2016, the average combined transfer value of the median MLS team (as estimated by the site Transfermarkt) was significantly lower than the average team in the first divisions in Mexico, Belgium, Portugal and the Netherlands. Since then, the league has essentially caught up to Belgium and Mexico in transfer value, and it has surpassed Portugal and the Netherlands.

Though the biggest teams in those European leagues are still way better and richer than any MLS side -- thanks to Champions League prize money -- the average match that Cavan Sullivan plays in MLS is probably tougher than what he'd face were he playing for Benfica, Porto or PSV.

All in all, the combined estimated transfer values of all 30 MLS clubs is €1.54 billion -- or about €51.3 million per team.

12 goals and assists
For the Big Five leagues, FBref has goal-and-assist data dating to at least the mid-1990s for Ligue 1, for the entirety of the Premier League since its breakaway from the English Football League in 1992, and the late 1980s for Italy, Germany and Spain.

Over that stretch, the record for goals+assists before a player's age-17 season comes from Bojan Krkic, who scored 10 goals and created three more in his early years -- right at the beginning of Pep Guardiola's dominance with Barcelona. Next after him is a tie between Yamal and Wayne Rooney's Everton years, at 10.

Sullivan currently has 12 -- a nearly even split between seven goals and five assists. If we expand the list out to the Next 14 leagues, then only four players have more. Chelsea's Estêvão registered 23 goal contributions with Palmeiras in Brazil's top flight -- a much tougher league than MLS. Normally, I'd remove penalties from the equation, but the fact that Estevao was chosen to take three penalties as a 16-year-old feels like useful information.

Then there's Adu with 22, Romelu Lukaku with 19 for Anderlecht, and Endrick's 15 with Palmeiras before he moved to Real Madrid.

The smart money is on Sullivan moving up the list over the next month as MLS wraps up its regular season. In his eight games since the World Cup, he has scored six goals and added four assists.

132 passes into the attacking third
Sullivan is the rare attacking prospect whose attacking production actually underrates his track record.

Of course, the production at this point in his career is fantastic -- bested only by a collection of some of the best attacking prospects of the past 30 years. But that production is backed up by a sustainable drumbeat of quality shots and chances created, plus a bedrock of excellent ball progression and off-ball movement.

To dig into some more advanced numbers, we need to move beyond FBref's historical database. Stats Perform doesn't have numbers that extend to the 1990s, but we're able to look at the Big Five in Europe, MLS, Liga MX, the Dutch Eredivisie, the English second division, a number of cup competitions in Europe and South America, plus the first divisions in Portugal, Brazil, Argentina and Colombia. The data dates to at least the mid-2010s.

Among all of the players who fall within there, Sullivan ranks third and second, respectively, in the two most important and predictive attacking metrics: expected goals and expected assists. The other players I've highlighted in the below chart, which only looks at minutes played at age 16 or earlier, mostly played in more difficult leagues, but across the modern era of the sport almost no one has done what Sullivan is currently doing, still eight years away from the start of his prime:

He's also not just standing up near the goal and waiting for things to happen. Among this same cohort, Sullivan leads all players in passes played into the attacking third, with 132. The only other players with more than 100 are Jude Bellingham (104) and Gilberto Mora (109), both of whom are midfielders, not attackers.

That's clear when we look at passes played into the penalty area. Both Mora and Bellingham landed right around 100; Sullivan is all the way up at 202. Only Yamal, at 254, played more.

Scoring goals, creating chances, moving the ball into the attacking third, moving the ball into the box -- that's all there. The only thing missing is an ability to find space off of the ball, and it's only missing because I haven't mentioned it yet.

Sullivan has taken 142 touches inside the box. Among this cohort, Yamal, again, is the only player with more.

78 rating
The best players in modern soccer are the wide attackers who score goals, create chances, move the ball into attacking positions and find space inside the box. The best attacking prospects -- players in their late teens and early 20s -- tend to be able to score and create goals at a young age, but that's it. They usually can't aid in buildup play -- outside of slowing things down with a succession of head-down dribbles that sometimes move the ball upfield but often kill attacks by allowing the defense to recover. And they rarely have an advanced enough understanding of space and ball movement to be patient and savvy enough to receive passes in dangerous positions.

This all-conquering winger is a new prototype of player -- so new that the two best examples, Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, are still playing. And so we haven't seen many young players develop with this idea in mind. That is, until Yamal -- and yes, now Sullivan.

The just-turned-17-year-old doesn't just have good-for-a-16-year-old numbers in his first real professional season. No, he genuinely has been one of the best players in MLS.

The player-rating model from the stats app Futi looks at how much every touch increases or decreases his team's chances of scoring and conceding a goal. Then it adjusts for the player's role and how well his team plays when he's on and off the field. And finally, they convert it all into an easy-to-understand 0-to-100 scale.

Among players with at least 1,500 minutes played this season, Sullivan currently ranks in the top 10 for the Futi model. The average age of the players ahead of him is nearly twice his: 31. And that's all for the full season; if we looked only at the post-World-Cup stretch, he probably would be even higher:

There are still plenty of questions.

Will he grow? What happens when he has moved beyond Philadelphia's relatively chaotic system? How might he handle moving and living in Europe? Those questions -- and more -- would hold true for any 16-year-old soccer player.

But while it probably won't happen because it's an unlikely outcome for everyone who has ever lived, Sullivan's early-career excellence means that he is more likely to become a superstar than any American who has come before him.

Just consider this. Futi also rates each individual area of a player's in-possession performance: shooting, creating, receiving, dribbling and linking (or buildup play). There are two players in the league who rate above a 60 in all five.

The two: Cavan Sullivan and Lionel Messi.

stories.headline: Crossland banned four games for Cleary tackle
stories.summary: Newcastle's Phoenix Crossland will miss the NRL grand final and most of the World Cup after receiving a four-match ban for his hip-drop tackle on Nathan Cleary.
stories.body:
Newcastle forward Phoenix Crossland apologised to "everyone" in rugby league as the NRL judiciary handed him a four-match ban for the hip-drop tackle that broke the leg of his favourite player, Penrith's Nathan Cleary.

During 85 minutes of evidence on Tuesday night at the NRL's Moore Park headquarters, Crossland said the incident had taken the focus off grand final week.

"Apologies to everyone involved in the game. I hope after tonight we can get back to the football," he said, holding back tears.

"If I could change the circumstances in any way, I would."

The suspension over the tackle in Newcastle's win over the Panthers in last Sunday's preliminary final, means Crossland will not only miss this Sunday's grand final against the Sydney Roosters but also the majority of the World Cup for New Zealand.

Crossland, who has played six Tests for New Zealand, will now miss all three pool games for the Kiwis against Australia, the Cook Islands and Fiji. New Zealand would have to make the semi-finals for him to feature.

The 26 year-old emerged from the hearing to make a statement without taking questions.

"I want to thank everybody inside for a fair hearing. I apologise to Nathan and the Panthers and more importantly to the game and the fans," he said.

"It's a terrible start to the most important week of the year due to myself.

"As soon as I walk out this building my focus goes to the Newcastle Knights and winning this grand final, helping Harrison Graham prepare as best he can and get a win on Sunday."

Graham stepped into the hooking role against the Panthers after Crossland was sent off and has been named on the bench for Sunday.

Crossland also revealed he had contacted Cleary and his father, Penrith coach Ivan Cleary, to apologise.

"It was a tough phone call and I just wanted to reach out and apologise," Crossland told Judiciary chair Geoffrey Bellew and panel members Ryan James and Paul Simpkins.

"It's been the worst couple of days of my life.

"He's my favourite player by a mile and the only reason he's in hospital is because of me.

"He was such a gentleman and told me not to worry and to stop saying sorry because these things just happen.

"He is a class act."

Knights counsel James McLeod had asked for a penalty of no more than three matches but said a two-game ban would be appropriate given Crossland had shown deep remorse and pleaded guilty.

NRL counsel Patrick Knowles SC said that while there were mitigating circumstances, a penalty of four matches was appropriate, comparing it to a four-game ban handed to St George Illawarra prop Ryan Couchman earlier this year.

His hip-drop tackle on Parramatta's J'maine Hopgood resulted in a season-ending ACL tear.

Cleary's injury was one of the worst suffered on an NRL field this season.

He underwent emergency surgery in Sydney's Royal North Shore Hospital on Sunday night.

Cleary is also Australia's incumbent halfback but will also miss the four-week World Cup, which starts on October 15.

The Knights submitted two character references for Crossland from 2001 premiership coach Michael Hagan and club legend Mark Hughes.

McLeod also drew attention to the fact Crossland had played 132 games for the Knights but never a grand final.

But Bellew said the game's judiciary code did not distinguish between matches.

"The fact a grand final will be missed is irrelevant," he said.

Crossland's 1077 tackles this year are the most of any player in the NRL, with the incident on Cleary only the second time he had been charged in 2026.

Tuesday night's decision came after Cleary called out those peppering the embattled Knight with social-media abuse and threats.

"Please don't be one of those people writing comments like this to Phoenix," Cleary posted alongside a graphic of some of the abuse Crossland had received.

"It was a complete accident and he doesn't deserve the unwarranted hate. He reached out to apologise and I have nothing but respect for him.

"He's a competitor and our game is made up of split-second moments that sometimes lead to unfortunate circumstances.

"Comments like this are so unfair. Spread love, not hate."

stories.headline: Fantasy baseball: Which hitters are MVPs, LVPs of 2026?
stories.summary: Eric Karabell looks back on the fantasy baseball season and hands out his MVPs and LVPs for hitters.
stories.body:
Fantasy managers saw what Chicago Cubs OF Pete Crow-Armstrong achieved in the first half of the 2025 season, when he was one of the top hitters in the game. Then came the final two months, as Crow-Armstrong delivered a .553 OPS with only four home runs, and it decreased his value. Crow-Armstrong still went in the sixth round of ESPN ADP for this season (No. 53), but investors could not be sure what statistics they were going to get.

What they got was the seventh 40-homer, 40-steal season in MLB history.

Crow-Armstrong started this season rather slowly, then he adjusted his mechanics and approach and, well, he became the best hitter/player in the sport. The numbers don't lie: Crow-Armstrong entered June hitting .237 with seven home runs. Then he hit .381 with 11 home runs in June and continued his assault on pitchers over the final few months. He blasted 14 home runs in August. He reached 40/40 in the closing games. This is the NL MVP -- and fantasy's MVP hitter as well.

As for the great Los Angeles Dodgers DH/SP Shohei Ohtani, it may be difficult for him to earn our nod for fantasy hitter MVP because he was the No. 1 pick in virtually every league. Monster numbers are always expected. Crow-Armstrong certainly wasn't some late-round steal (and we have some listed below), but a sixth-round choice going 40/40 is massive value. Ohtani pitched like a Cy Young Award winner for a while and the hitting numbers were there, but then he stopped pitching, struggled at the plate and ended up hitting the IL as the season approached its final weeks.

Other MVP hitter candidates
Yordan Alvarez, DH/OF, Houston Astros: Fantasy managers did not forget that Alvarez was a terrific offensive option for four seasons prior to missing most of the 2025 campaign due to several injuries. A third-round pick in 2026 ADP, Alvarez sure bounced back and then some, delivering his best season and a likely AL MVP award. Alvarez posted career bests with 158 games, a .316 batting average, 42 home runs, 106 RBIs, 105 runs and 109 walks. He finished fifth on the overall Player Rater, third among hitters.

Jordan Walker, OF, St. Louis Cardinals: Once a top prospect, Walker hit a sad .215 with six home runs in 2025. He made changes in his approach and ended up as arguably the top bargain of 2026, considering he went undrafted (No. 458 ADP) in almost every league. He hit .269 with 29 home runs, 102 RBIs and 22 steals -- and he won the midseason Home Run Derby. Despite a tepid second half, Walker still finished 17th overall on the Rater. He should be a fantasy building block for years to come.

Miguel Vargas, 3B/1B, Chicago White Sox: Vargas also went undrafted (No. 255 ADP) in most fantasy leagues after posting a .717 OPS with 16 home runs during the 2025 season. Then he blossomed into a legitimate star, hitting 33 home runs, scoring 106 runs and even stealing 22 bases as the White Sox made the playoffs. Vargas finished 23rd on the Rater and was fifth among hitters in points formats.

Kevin McGonigle, SS/3B, Detroit Tigers: This talented rookie went in the Vargas range of drafts (No. 250), if he went at all in your league. What happened next? In case you didn't notice, he ended up as a top-10 hitter in points formats and No. 32 in roto/categories. Not too shabby.

Jake McCarthy, OF, Colorado Rockies: There was little reason to invest in McCarthy prior to the season, but then he became a starter for the Rockies and delivered a top-tier outfielder season. No, really. McCarthy was the No. 7 outfielder this season -- a five-category provider in roto formats.

Honorable mention: Alec Burleson, OF/1B/DH, Cardinals; Otto Lopez, SS/2B, Miami Marlins; Sal Stewart, 1B/3B/DH, Cincinnati Reds; Luis Garcia Jr., 2B/1B/DH, New York Yankees/Washington Nationals; Jake Bauers, 1B/3B, Milwaukee Brewers; Carson Benge, OF, New York Mets.

2026's fantasy LVP hitters
Aaron Judge, OF, Yankees: Volume matters, and Judge, the consensus No. 2 pick in ESPN leagues after Ohtani, participated in only 66 games. That's it. Fantasy managers did not get what they expected after Judge appeared in 152 and 158 games the prior two seasons. He wasn't the only top hitter to miss significant playing time due to injury (Juan Soto, Jose Ramirez, Ronald Acuna Jr.) -- it was that kind of fantasy season. Still, the good news is this: Alvarez was last season's LVP hitter (48 games) and he did OK this time around.

Cal Raleigh, C, Seattle Mariners: Fantasy managers were warned that investing in a catcher -- any catcher -- to build a fantasy offense around is a dangerous practice. Catchers get hurt and often they play through injury and their numbers suffer as a result. After an amazing 2025 season (60 HR), Raleigh never got going in 2026, hitting just .182 with 23 home runs.

Dishonorable mention: Vladimir Guerrero Jr., 1B, Toronto Blue Jays; Francisco Lindor, SS, Mets; Gunnar Henderson, SS, Baltimore Orioles; Roman Anthony, OF, Boston Red Sox; Brent Rooker, OF/DH, Athletics.

stories.headline: How Fever's Kelsey Mitchell juggles pursuit of WNBA title, Ph.D.
stories.summary: The Fever guard is having a historic season and the best year of her career, all while pursuing a doctorate degree.
stories.body:
INDIANA -- Kelsey Mitchell's eyes darted back and forth as she figured out how to tackle the task. She needed to write only 150 words and scrolled through the online portal for her doctorate program. Her eyes finally landed on a prompt that sparked her fingers to fly furiously across the keyboard.

Similar to many assignments, she combined her two worlds.

"I actually use the Indiana Fever in my classes a lot," Mitchell told ESPN, still typing away. "That's the cheat code to being an athlete currently and being able to be in school. A lot of real-life situations that I utilize while playing with the Fever, I take them and apply them to discussion posts and papers."

Mitchell is 18 months into her pursuit of a Ph.D. in educational leadership at Liberty University. She is also enjoying the best season of her nine-year WNBA career, ranking second in the league in scoring behind MVP front-runner A'ja Wilson and trying to lead the Fever to the franchise's second championship. On Tuesday, with Indiana on the brink of elimination in the WNBA playoffs, that means finding a way to beat Wilson's Aces in Game 2 of the first round.

For most, it might seem to be a lot to juggle as Mitchell toggles between team and term papers and professors and professional basketball. She plans to use her doctorate to be an athletic director one day; she wants to ensure that more women and people of color are in decision-making roles.

But the role she plays for the Fever and what she hopes to do in the next stage of life go hand in hand, both rooted in Mitchell's endless pursuit to help those around her. One goal is to help lead the next generation of student-athletes, and the other is bringing a title back to Indiana for the first time since 2012. She takes the lessons she learns on the court or in the classroom and applies them to one another.

"Everything that I'm learning in terms of leading and using it in different rooms of life -- on the court and off the court -- I know for a fact I am giving [those lessons] to someone else," Mitchell said. "Even if I don't see it yet, I know somebody else can take what I have and be able to use it for themselves."

MITCHELL ABRUPTLY STOPPED walking in the middle of the decisive game of the WNBA semifinals last year. She clutched onto the referee as he walked beside her, trying to steady herself, but her body went limp. As she collapsed, the referee gently lowered her to the floor; she later said she couldn't feel her legs for over five seconds.

Mitchell was diagnosed with rhabdomyolysis, a medical condition where her muscles stopped functioning after working too hard. "I played literally til my wheels fell off," she wrote afterward in a post on social media.

The terrifying moment was the lasting image of Mitchell's 2025 season, and it also captured her tendency to put everything she has into the task in front of her.

"Sometimes, you are just in awe. She never gets tired. She just goes and goes, and she doesn't talk about it; she just does it," Fever coach Stephanie White said. " When you see someone do that, instinctually, as a teammate, you don't want to let them down. She is giving everything she has. She is playing her a-- off ... when you have that example, you don't want to be the one who is dogging it."

At 30 years old, Mitchell is playing the best basketball of her career. This season, she scored at least 20 points in 27 consecutive games, setting a WNBA record. She averaged a franchise-record 24.7 points, fourth best in WNBA history.

Drafted by the Fever in 2018 with the No. 2 pick, Mitchell is the longest-tenured player on the roster. She has been with the organization through a handful of iterations, from a rebuild project that tallied single-digit victories in four of Mitchell's first five seasons to one of the most talked-about teams in the league.

The turnaround hit full throttle when Indiana drafted Aliyah Boston and Caitlin Clark with consecutive No. 1 picks in 2023 and 2024. As Boston anchors the frontcourt, the backcourt of Clark and Mitchell became one of the best duos in the WNBA, combining for 47.0 points per game in the regular season, the most by a duo in a season in WNBA history (Clark ranked third in the league, behind Wilson and Mitchell).

"Over the course of the season, you have seen them get more comfortable and you've seen them grow," White said. "[Caitlin] is playing in more areas of the court than she has in the past. Kelsey is getting easier looks at times because of how C is getting her the ball. And vice versa. That's their continued willingness to stretch themselves."

They've established a lethal two-woman game, too, with Clark recording 94 assists to Mitchell -- tied for the second most by one player to another during the regular season. Both thrive with the ball, but they recognize the benefits of playing together and finding the right balance.

"You have to keep the ego out of it," Mitchell said. "For us to be as great as we want to be, we have to make sure we are always open for and to one another. And honestly, we have to be vulnerable to one another."

Mitchell showed that kind of maturity and leadership when Clark and her star power first arrived.

"I think, at times, I could be a little bit of an intimidating thing when I first came here, but it never came across that way," Clark said. "She always was happy for me [and] happy with everything that has come with me being in Indiana."

Clark is quick to credit Mitchell for Indiana's run to the semifinals last season, when injuries ravaged the Fever roster and limited Clark to 13 games, and called Mitchell "the best scorer in the league." Last season, Mitchell averaged 20.2 points and led the Fever to their first winning season since 2015. This season, she led the league in 3-point field goal percentage (45.0%) and was tied for second in made 3-pointers (3.1). She is also just the second player to score at least 1,000 points in a season in WNBA history, joining Wilson.

"It's incredible. She's playing her best basketball now," Clark said. "She has been through some really rough seasons with the Fever. She has always been a tremendous hooper, but they didn't find ways to win, so it's been fun to get a lot of these wins for her. She deserves it."

IT WAS PUSHING 11 p.m. when Mitchell and the Fever boarded the team plane after Indiana's loss in New York on Aug. 22. In less than 24 hours, they would face the Sky in Chicago, so almost everyone onboard was hoping to rest on the 2-hour, 45-minute flight.

Except for Mitchell. She had less than an hour to turn in an assignment by the 11:59 p.m. deadline.

"Imagine looking at that clock and being like, 'OK, so I got 59 minutes,'" Mitchell said. "Like, 'Oh, no pressure' ... it's kind of tough, but I love it."

Mitchell's parents always emphasized the importance of education. Her mother, Cheryl, was a social worker, and her late father, Mark, was a high school teacher and basketball coach with a master's degree in physical education.

When Mark died suddenly in 2024, it deeply impacted Mitchell. Mark had coached her throughout her childhood and encouraged her to get her master's degree, which she did in sports administration in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic and WNBA bubble season. When she realized her education might not be done, Mark reminded his daughter there was no reason she couldn't continue to pursue higher education as long as she could find a way to balance her job and school.

Mitchell never told her teammates that she was back in school, but they quickly picked up on it. When the team reported for training camp ahead of the 2025 season, Mitchell carried her laptop everywhere, setting up mini workstations whenever she got the chance.

"If she is not playing basketball or working out, she is doing homework," Indiana's Sophie Cunningham told ESPN. "If this is how she's going to play while trying to get a Ph.D., she needs to get multiple. Keep lining them up, sister."

Every morning, Mitchell checks a color-coded schedule that has her day planned out in different blocks -- practice, weightlifting and intense schoolwork. But her studying rarely stays confined to the time block dedicated to it. Mitchell typically finds pockets of time after practice to squeeze in an assignment. Before games, she sits at her locker and works for as long as she can before she has to turn her attention to the game. Plane rides now have become study hall.

"Her ability to compartmentalize all of these things and show up every single day; she doesn't act stressed, doesn't act anxious," Fever guard Lexie Hull said. "It's just insane that she's able to [study so hard] and then switch her mind and perform as she does on the court. It's the most impressive thing I've ever seen."

Mitchell takes two classes per semester; the most recent one started four weeks ago. She completed two courses last year and has eight more to go, all of which are electives that are needed to fill out the completion plan. After that, Mitchell begins the dissertation process, which includes a thesis paper that ranges from 100 to 300 pages. She estimates it will take another 18 months to earn her doctorate degree.

"I'm going to slow-walk through it, but I like that I'm doing it on purpose this way. I don't want it to interfere with what I love most, which is basketball," Mitchell said. "I like that I get the chance to achieve something while competing. It's a [new level of] discipline. It's a sacrifice I will keep making."

MITCHELL HAS ALWAYS been a woman of few words. Her leadership in Indiana has evolved, and her game is better than ever, but she leads with her actions.

"She is never going to be super, super loud or a constant vocal person, but when she does speak, everyone shuts up and listens to her," Clark said. "She continues to show up for her team. She loves on her teammates really hard. ... It's easy to follow [her] lead."

As the Fever struggled through her first four seasons, Mitchell believed her leadership was based on keeping everyone in the locker room positive and bought into what the organization was trying to do. When Hull and NaLyssa Smith were drafted in 2022, they looked at Mitchell as the vet, pulling her into a bigger role. As Boston brought a bigger vocal presence and Clark became the face of the franchise, Mitchell never resented the leadership positions they took on. If anything, they allowed her to thrive.

"I try to lead with an ego-less heart," Mitchell said. "Anything I try to do when leading is just pouring in and giving back."

While her pursuit of a Ph.D. is geared toward something beyond basketball, Mitchell feels herself growing within the Fever even more as she studies what it means to be a good teacher and advocate -- her two worlds again feeding each other and making her better prepared to tackle each job.

"Together, I just feel myself turning over new leaves that I didn't know that I needed," Mitchell said. "Being able to compromise, sacrifice and kind of be whatever I need to be on the floor. I've learned a lot. And so they both kind of jell together."

stories.headline: Fernando Alonso, 45, extends F1 career by signing new contract at Aston Martin
stories.summary: Fernando Alonso will race into his 24th season in Formula 1 after signing a new contract at Aston Martin.
stories.body:
Fernando Alonso will remain at Aston Martin next season after the team confirmed the two-time world champion will continue alongside teammate Lance Stroll in 2027.

Alonso, 45, who made his Formula 1 debut in 2001, had been weighing up his future this year after Aston Martin and its engine partner Honda made a slow start under the sport's controversial new technical regulations for 2026.

Aston Martin always maintained the door was open for Alonso to continue at the team in 2027, but it took until Tuesday for the Spaniard to confirm his decision.

"I took my time to make this decision, but racing is my life, my passion, and I know I still have the speed and determination to compete at the highest level," Alonso said. "I'm committed for the long term with this team and to helping us succeed.

"I truly believe in what we are building: we have strong leadership, incredible people, partners and facilities. I look forward to making more memories on the race track in front of the passionate fans. Their energy creates an atmosphere that inspires me and is what makes our sport special."

Alonso's commitment to Aston Martin for 2027 was announced alongside news that Stroll -- the son of Aston Martin owner Lawrence Stroll -- will also remain at the team.

"Lance and Fernando have been a crucial part of our journey and we are very pleased to confirm that they will continue with us into the next chapter for the team," Lawrence Stroll said. "Having two drivers with their level of experience, commitment and knowledge provides tremendous value to the whole organisation.

"We are here to win, and whilst our short-term focus remains on improving performance, I believe we have the world-class talent we need to achieve our long-term objectives."

In an interview with BBC Sport, Alonso said his decision was partly motivated by his belief that he, as a driver, is still capable of fighting with the very best on the grid, even if his car in not fast enough to regularly compete for points.

"When I jump in the car, in free practice, I will see some people braking late in a corner, locking up the front tyres here or there, making mistakes there," Alonso said.

"I feel that I'm OK. Or, I'm faster than them.

"So when I get changed and I go back home, even if I'm P18, in a way I feel some satisfaction and pride inside, even if it should not be the case because we are not competitive.

"How will I be in the living room, watching TV, thinking that I can do better? That will be my feeling now. When that changes, if I see that I lost abilities, I lost speed, I lost reflexes, I lost something, then I will be happy to watch from my living room the race.

"At the moment, I feel it was not the time because I'm better than that guy. I'm better than that other guy. I will think like that. And I cannot stop racing if I still think like that."

- Norris apologises to Colapinto after ban demand

- Ferrari gives Vasseur 'full confidence' amid Horner speculation

- Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia 2026: Race start time, how to watch

In the same interview, Alonso made clear that he still has faith in Aston Martin's ability to provide a competitive car next year.

The team, which is led by legendary designer Adrian Newey, brought a significant upgrade to the Hungarian Grand Prix this year, while Honda introduced an updated engine at the Dutch Grand Prix.

Aston Martin remains at the back of the field -- and struggled throughout last weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix in Baku -- but Alonso believes next year will bring a step forward in performance.

"This team has all the ingredients to have success in the future and I didn't feel that this was the moment to leave," Alonso added. "It was the moment to keep on going, giving a second chance to Honda as well to fix their problems as well and stay together with the team.

"Adrian was probably the biggest contributor to this. We didn't start it right this year but things are moving in the right direction and he's capable of changing things very quickly.

"Aston is my family. I know Lawrence and Lance for many, many years. We keep open conversations, many different topics, every week. And that will be the case also for next year.

"There are no guarantees that next year the engine will be completely fixed but all the changes that are happening in Honda made sense, so I have faith.

"The trust that I have in the team, it didn't change even throughout this difficult year. In the future, I don't know how long it's going to take, but it will be a successful team, and I want to be part of it."

Alonso has been among the biggest critics of F1's new regulations for 2026, which put added emphasis on energy management.

Earlier this season, the Aston Martin driver labelled the latest iteration of the sport a "battery world championship" and highlighted the regulations as one of the factors that could convince him to retire.

However, targeted changes to the regulations over the next two years appear to have softened his stance, and he is hopeful the racing will improve.

"This year, there have been some good races and some bad races," Alonso told BBC Sport. "Maybe some of the shorter circuits that you had the battery until the braking point are changing the way you perceive the driving.

"And some of the circuits like Silverstone, Spa, Suzuka, they were very bad, you know, because they derate and things like that.

"Maybe even for next year they can tweak a little bit the battery power to have a little bit maybe less battery for longer or something like that because F1 at the moment is not natural driving.

"Reaching the top speed in the middle of the straight, it goes against the driver instinct of braking late and going on power earlier. It seems that if you want to drive these cars fast, you ended up going slower and that's not the way it should be."

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Liverpool keen on Real Madrid midfielder Tchouaméni
stories.summary: Liverpool have maintained contact with the representatives of Real Madrid midfielder Aurélien Tchouaméni. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Real Madrid midfielder Aurélien Tchouaméni is still on the radar of Liverpool, while Internazionale are eyeing a January move for USMNT and Crystal Palace defender Chris Richards. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Liverpool have maintained contact with the representatives of Real Madrid midfielder Aurélien Tchouaméni despite the 26-year-old signing a new deal until 2031, according to TEAMtalk. While the Reds are not actively pursuing the France international right now, they could revive their interest if his role under José Mourinho changes given he has only played three times so far this season. Madrid had reportedly been willing to listen to offers of around €80 million over the summer.

- Internazionale are eyeing a January move for USMNT and Crystal Palace defender Chris Richards, according to Tuttosport. Inter scouts have been tracking the 26-year-old, who operates on the right side of Palace's back three, as part of the club's plan to bring in free agents. Richards' contract expires in 2027 and he could bolster a defense already containing new arrivals Djed Spence and John Stones.

stories.headline: NHL betting guide: 32 teams, 32 bets to make this season
stories.summary: One bet to make on each of the NHL's 32 squads, including Stanley Cup winner, player awards and more futures.
stories.body:
The NHL drops the puck on a new season Tuesday night, and with every team playing 84 games, it will be the biggest season yet. As 32 teams enter the season with renewed optimism and reshuffled rosters, we have what sports bettors can look forward to this season with one futures bet to make for every team. Sean Allen and Victoria Matiash have the betting insight for every team, including awards races, playoff chases and player milestones.

The Carolina Hurricanes open the season as co-favorites to repeat, but will they be a good bet to do so? Also, which players have betting value when it comes to the Norris Trophy, Vezina Trophy and Calder Trophy? From Jack Hughes prop bets to Quinn Hughes prop bets and everything in between, here are the 32 best bets to make for the NHL season.

Sean Allen made his best bets for the Eastern Conference, and Victoria Matiash for the Western Conference. All odds provided by DraftKings and are accurate as of publish time.

Jump ahead: Anaheim | Boston | Buffalo | Calgary | Carolina | Chicago

Colorado | Columbus | Dallas | Detroit | Edmonton | Florida | Los Angeles | Minnesota

Montreal | Nashville | New Jersey | NY Islanders | NY Rangers | Ottawa | Philadelphia | Pittsburgh

San Jose | Seattle | St. Louis | Tampa Bay | Toronto | Utah

Vancouver | Vegas | Washington | Winnipeg

Anaheim Ducks

Anaheim Ducks To Miss Playoffs (+120): Chris Kreider is now in Montreal. Mason McTavish is over in St. Louis. Out for weeks to start the season, Troy Terry is hurt. Anaheim's blue line appears radically different, with experienced defensemen Jacob Trouba, Radko Gudas and John Carlson gone elsewhere. This isn't the same team that clinched a playoff spot this past season and, on paper, they're not better. Unlike the San Jose Sharks, who seem poised to replace Anaheim amongst the top four in the Pacific. Which may not even suffice, if five teams advance from the Central.

Boston Bruins

Charlie McAvoy, Norris Trophy Winner (25-1): McAvoy set up the power-play offense at a top-15 rate per minute while logging a team-high 24-plus minutes a night. He's the distribution engine on a thin blue line, and a full season in his prime could have him in the conversation for best blue-liner. The volume of minutes is the edge.

Buffalo Sabres

Tage Thompson to Record 50+ Regular Season Goals (10-1): No, he's never had 50 in a season before, but 47 in 78 games was a solid run in 2022-23. His 40-goal campaign last season was actually a 43-goal pace if you toss out his seven-game slow start. Now remember that it's an 84-game regular season and Thompson is in his prime.

Calgary Flames

Dustin Wolf to Record 30+ Regular Season Wins (+230): Banking on breakout performances from youngsters like Zayne Parekh and Matvei Gridin, and bounce-back showings from veteran Jonathan Huberdeau (once that hip is fully healed) and others, the Flames might not be as bad as last season. If so, and Wolf starts about 60 of 84 games, 30 victories is achievable.

Carolina Hurricanes

Carolina to Win The Stanley Cup (+650): They didn't lose much, if anything, in the offseason and Seth Jarvis has plenty of time to recover. Why not get in on the ground floor for a Hurricanes dynasty? Especially if they actually manage to use Alexander Nikishin as leverage to be in on the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes.

Chicago Blackhawks

Patrick Kane to Record 20+ Regular Season Goals (+100): They don't call him "Showtime" for nothing. In his return to Chicago, Kane stands to put up some fairly impressive numbers on a top line and power play with Connor Bedard, once the star center returns in early November. Feeling and moving the best he has in some time, Kane is capable of scoring 30-plus goals in anything resembling a full campaign. He's only one season removed from potting 21 in 72 contests in Detroit.

Colorado Avalanche

Martin Necas & Nathan MacKinnon to Record a Combined 215+ Regular Season Points (+100): This dynamic duo piled up 227 points in 158 contests in 2025-26. Now they have up to 168 total games to bang out 215. For plus-money, it's an appealing proposition for two historically durable skaters.

Columbus Blue Jackets

Columbus to Make The Playoffs (+150): The offseason was touch-and-go, with Zach Werenski musing about a departure and Kirill Marchenko traded to Toronto, but everyone that matters is back, Adam Fantilli is set to level up and Valeri Nichushkin is a game-changing change-of-scenery bet. Why can't they push for a wild-card spot?

Dallas Stars

Jason Robertson to Record 45+ Regular Season Goals (+140): He scored 45 in 82 games this past season while competing on an expiring contract. Now, betting on himself with a fresh one-year deal, the 27-year-old has two extra games to hit the same mark.

Detroit Red Wings

Lucas Raymond to Record 80+ Regular Season Points (+110): Raymond set up goals at a top-30 rate per minute and inherits more of the offense with Patrick Kane gone. Averaging sub-19 minutes per game in his career, he has minutes to add to an 84-game pace of 78 points across the past three seasons combined.

Edmonton Oilers

Evan Bouchard to Record 90+ Regular Season Points (+110): He collected 95 points in 82 contests this past campaign. If there's a puck-moving defenseman who can reach 100 in an 84-game stretch, Bouchard may serve as the biggest threat as power-play mate to Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl. Durable as they come, the 26-year-old has only missed two regular-season matches in the past five years.

Florida Panthers

Jacob Markstrom to Record 30+ Regular Season Wins (+380): The way this Florida team stacks on paper with the addition of Brady Tkachuk and return of Aleksander Barkov should allow for any goaltender that appears in 50 games to win 30 of them. Markstrom just needs to stay healthy to meet this bar.

Los Angeles Kings

Drew Doughty to Record 35+ Regular Season Points (+135): While his halcyon days with the extra skater are admittedly in the rearview, Doughty registered only one point of 23 in 30 games on the power play this past season. Even with Brandt Clarke taking over the lion's share of special teams' minutes, the single point feels anomalously low for someone who's still competing with the man-advantage. Doughty has averaged 0.55 points/game throughout his illustrious career. Slapped with the "C" ahead of 2026-27, the 36-year-old isn't that long in the tooth yet.

Minnesota Wild

Kirill Kaprizov and Quinn Hughes to Record a Combined 180+ Regular Season Points (+170): This is essentially a wager on the health of both skaters. Kaprizov has averaged 1.24 points/game since his first full season In Minnesota. If the winger plays 79 of 84 contests, that translates into 98. Leaving Hughes to account for 82 himself. The star defenseman is projected to collect between 82 and 86, so that adds up well.

Montreal Canadiens

Cole Caufield and Nick Suzuki to Record a Combined 200+ Regular Season Points (+850): Betting on the up-and-coming Canadiens offense to take another step up does not seem unreasonable. They combined for 189 points last season, get an extra two games to play with the new schedule and should see a new level for Ivan Demidov's creativity with them on the power play. They don't have to both earn triple-digits here; just combine for 200.

Nashville Predators

Ross Colton to Record 30+ Regular Season Points (+115): The last time Colton moved from one organization to another -- traveling from Tampa Bay to Colorado for the 2022-23 season -- he collected 40 points in 80 games. Keen to make a good first impression once again in Nashville, Colton will be afforded the opportunity to contribute from the third line with Jonathan Marchessault and secondary power play. Thirty points isn't a big ask at all.

New Jersey Devils

Jack Hughes to Record 110+ Regular Season Points (25-0): This has got to be it, right? The season Hughes manages to stay on the ice for the whole campaign? If he does, 110 points will be a cake walk. He led all players in March and April with 38 points, which is a 147-point pace over an 84-game schedule. Heck, at that rate, he can even miss a few games.

New York Islanders

Matthew Schaefer, Norris Trophy Winner (16-1): Bold, but the profile's real. Schaefer stepped straight into top-pairing, power-play minutes as a rookie and produced all season. This one gets real traction if the Islanders' power play gets out of the league basement.

New York Rangers

Mika Zibanejad and Pavel Dorofeyev to Record a Combined 65+ Regular Season Goals (+110): The Rangers may have bolder goals, like getting back into the playoff mix, but no matter the team trajectory, this power play remains as dangerous as ever, especially with the addition of Dorofeyev. They actually combined for more than 70 goals last season, but let's shave a few off because they can't both get credit for all the power-play tallies.

Ottawa Senators

Drake Batherson, to Record 100+ Regular Season Points (28-1): OK, yes, he had only 71 points last season, so this would be adding 30 -- a tall order to be sure. With Brady Tkachuk gone to Florida, someone absorbs the man-advantage load and Batherson already produced at a top-20 power-play rate per minute. He's the finisher poised to inherit more.

Philadelphia Flyers

Porter Martone, Calder Trophy Winner (+280): Chalky, yes. But chalky for a reason. He showed everything we need to see in his nine-game sample at the end of last season, with tons of shots, plenty of scoring and power-play acumen.

Pittsburgh Penguins

Sidney Crosby to Record 90+ Regular Season Points (+300): Give the captain his due: Crosby set up goals at a top-25 rate per minute and hasn't slowed, even as the roster around him churns. He remains the offense's straw that stirs it. A points total set to Pittsburgh's middling team outlook undersells that he'll still be feeding scorers.

San Jose Sharks

Macklin Celebrini, Hart Trophy Winner (+450): MacKinnon plays with Cale Makar. McDavid competes with Draisaitl. If he nears 115 points again and helps drag his Sharks into the postseason for the first time since 2019, Celebrini will be in heavy consideration for the award honoring the most valuable to his team. No other skater in San Jose even hit 60 points in 2025-26.

Seattle Kraken

Kraken to Finish the Regular Season with the Fewest Standings Points (+425): There's a fresher feeling in Vancouver, where the Canucks are expected to benefit from an overhaul in management and fresh voice behind the bench. With emerging young talent and bounce-back performances anticipated from some veterans, the Flames may serve as somewhat of a pleasant surprise this season. That leaves the Kraken, who, despite management's best efforts to attract high-end talent, as a realistic candidate to tumble to the bottom of the NHL's weakest division, and league standings altogether.

St. Louis Blues

Jimmy Snuggerud to Record 30+ Regular Season Goals (+600): Tapped as one the league's top potential breakout candidate, Snuggerud is projected to substantially build on his rookie tally of 51 points in 70 games. On a top line and power play with Robert Thomas, he could score 40 goals. Which makes this 30-plus offer all the more appealing.

Tampa Bay Lightning

Andrei Vasilevskiy, Vezina Trophy Winner (+800): If you're backing a goalie award, Vasilevskiy's the ironman to do it on as he's elite, durable, and on a strong defensive team that funnels him volume. Wins and workload are what Vezina voters reward, and he is one of the few goalies that checks both.

Toronto Maple Leafs

Auston Matthews to Record 55+ Regular Season Goals (12-1): Rather than chasing the award futures on Rocket Richard Trophy at 10-1, add a little more return for specificity in Matthews getting back on track as one of the league's premiere scorers. He was still a top-10 shooter on rate last season, he just needs his health to cooperate.

Utah Mammoth

Dylan Guenther to Record 40+ Regular Season Goals (+215): At age 22, and still improving, he scored 40 in 79 games this past season. While Guenther's shooting percentage (16.5%) registered a bit high, having up to five additional games this year arguably serves as adequate compensation.

Vancouver Canucks

Vancouver Canucks Under 74.5 Regular Season Points (-110): The Canucks will likely register more than the 58 points earned last season, but not that many more. New GM Ryan Johnson, along with the rest of his management team, is playing the long-game. There's no pressing sense of urgency. On paper, Vancouver's squad is the weakest in the league and there are only so many points to go around. If they accumulate 70 by April 10, that will be viewed as a step in the right direction.

Vegas Golden Knights

Vegas Golden Knights Pacific Division Champion (+185): Before competition gets underway, the Pacific Division crown feels like a two-team race between the Golden Knights and Oilers. Considering how the goaltending situation appears more suspect in Edmonton than Vegas, and the uncertainty of how new coach Mike Babcock will gel with his new charges week over week, siding with Ryan Craig's experienced crew strikes as the safer bet.

Washington Capitals

Cole Hutson, Calder Trophy Winner (+950): While everyone is distracted by Martone, Gavin McKenna or the other rookie forwards, look to the blue line. It's a small sample, but Hutson led the league in power-play points per minute (on just 14 games). Small-sample rates regress, yet the underlying role if he can quarterback a loaded, Alex Ovechkin-laden unit is real and sticky.

Winnipeg Jets

Winnipeg Jets to Record 90+ Regular Season Points (+130): Before eking out a measly 82, the Jets recorded 116 points -- good enough for the Presidents' Trophy -- the previous season. According to general consensus, the current realistic expectation for this not-spectacular-but-not-that-terrible club probably lies near the arithmetic mean, which is 99. Ninety points in 84 games feels very doable, even without Connor Hellebuyck.

stories.headline: Fantasy basketball: Eric Karabell's 'Do Draft' list
stories.summary: Eric Karabell highlights the players who are falling further than they should be in fantasy basketball drafts this season.
stories.body:
When the much-maligned Julius Randle was the best player for the New York Knicks, before, you know, they eagerly jettisoned him toward the Minnesota Timberwolves in the Karl-Anthony Towns trade and won an NBA championship, he was one of the more underrated fantasy options around. I would marvel at how Randle consistently would be available outside the top 50 of drafts, despite numbers that clearly warranted better. After all, in our game, the numbers are what matters.

Remember, starting with the 2020-21 season, when Randle earned the league's Most Improved Player award, he averaged 23.2 PPG, 10.0 RPG and 5.1 APG for three Knicks seasons. He was durable, appearing in 71 or more games each season, and he led the league with 37.6 MPG that first year. No, we didn't always enjoy the shooting and turnovers, but this wasn't a top 25 option in drafts, either. Randle earned two All-Star selections, and from a fantasy aspect, routinely outperformed his ADP in fantasy drafts.

Get ready for more of that version of Randle, because the Timberwolves dumped his contract on the Brooklyn Nets this offseason, and the big numbers are coming back. They must! The Nets, if you haven't noticed, are not exactly loaded. Randle and Michael Porter Jr. will get all the usage they desire. They will score the points and, assuming they feel like it, garner myriad rebounds, too. Randle should feel like it. His usage will skyrocket. The Nets may not win much, but fantasy managers don't care. Randle, 31, should deliver the solid statistics we recall from his Knicks days and, looking at early ADP, few seem terribly interested.

Randle's efforts haven't always helped his NBA teams to much success -- the Knicks won a single playoff series in his five seasons, he played a lesser role for last season's Timberwolves, and he missed the playoffs with the Los Angeles Lakers and New Orleans Pelicans -- but the numbers helped us, the greedy fantasy managers. Randle is a top 50 fantasy option, but sans that level of draft day commitment. Go get him.

Welcome to the latest "Do Draft" list for fantasy basketball. I do this every season, highlighting players I feel warrant earlier attention as related to their general ADP. We know ADP varies by site, but we can tell who potential managers target and those they do not. Consider durability, age, role and other factors, of course, but sometimes the risk is worth the reward. In addition to Randle, here are others that should be getting picked earlier in drafts.

James Harden, PG/SG, Cleveland Cavaliers: We are seeing a larger range of ADP possibilities than typical for Harden but, even if goes early in Round 2, he is worth it! Harden, 37, has never really failed to produce numbers. Worried about durability? He played in more than 70 games each of the past three seasons. He scores, passes, hits free throws and plays.

Jalen Johnson, PF, Atlanta Hawks: Johnson took a big step forward last season when he averaged 22.5 PPG, 10.3 RPG and 7.9 APG. A certain Denver Nuggets MVP center is the only other player to achieve all those numbers. I aim to build fantasy teams around point guards and power forwards, and when the power forward piles on assists as well and tends to slip to Round 2, that is special.

Domantas Sabonis, C/PF, Sacramento Kings: As with Randle, Sabonis may not play for a team expected to win much, but that's not our problem. Sabonis is a three-time rebounding champion who scores 19 PPG each season and contributes more assists than most every frontcourt option. You may need to secure his services in Round 2, but that is reasonable considering his talent.

Alperen Sengun, C, Houston Rockets: Sengun isn't Nikola Jokic either, but any player averaging 20 PPG, 9 RPG and 6 APG is a building block option. I have seen Sengun fall in several drafts, mocks and otherwise, and it is a mistake.

Evan Mobley, PF/C, Cleveland Cavaliers: OK, so it is time for me to stop predicting Mobley, still only 25, will finally emerge to average 20 PPG and 10 RPG. He probably could do so on most teams, but instead he delivers solid, consistent numbers just short of that, along with blocked shots. Only 13 players averaged 1.5 BPG last season, and a certain San Antonio Spurs future MVP center was the only one to average both more points and rebounds than Mobley. This is a solid fourth-round selection.

Ivica Zubac, C, Indiana Pacers: Face it, Zubac simply had a lost season for the Clippers and Pacers. However, nobody hauled in more rebounds during the 2024-25 campaign. Zubac routinely piles on rebounds, shoots 60% from the field and before last season when circumstances dictated otherwise, he played regularly. I'm not sure if I like the current aggressive Tyrese Haliburton ADP coming off a torn Achilles (though he may pile on the assists like Trae Young, in theory), but Zubac after the top 50 is solid.

Austin Reaves, SG/PG, Los Angeles Lakers: Some will question if Reaves, the team's No. 2 option after a certain Hall of Famer (the leading scorer in NBA history) left town for Philadelphia, will improve on his numbers. Must he improve them? Reaves scores, rebounds, passes and hits 3-pointers, and good luck finding a volume 3-point option shooting 49% overall from the field.

Stephon Castle, PG/SG, San Antonio Spurs: Castle's numbers in Year 2 showed growth in every aspect, and even with the likely emergence of barely younger Dylan Harper, we should expect more production ahead, especially for scoring and 3-point shooting. Castle is a responsible guard who rebounds and steals. When he starts shooting more, we should get 20 PPG, too.

Darius Garland, PG, LA Clippers: I constantly covet point guards who slip in drafts, and Garland's early ADP figures are lacking. There is little reason why, on this team, he cannot return to his days of 20-plus PPG and 7.5 APG, with steals and 3-pointers. Pass in Round 5, but Garland is going considerably later than that and it makes little sense.

Kel'el Ware, C, Milwaukee Bucks: Ware's second season went better than the first, as he flirted with averaging a double-double, he shot well and he contributed blocked shots and steals, but his role wasn't fluid. In fact, Ware averaged barely 22 MPG. That number should go way up with the rebuilding Bucks, who covet his defensive presence. Honestly, by the time we get to Round 8 or so, ADP doesn't matter much to me. If you really want a player and it is that late, don't wait!

Naz Reid, C/PF, Charlotte Hornets: As with Randle, Reid is no longer competing with selfish Timberwolves C Rudy Gobert for rebounds. Reid is a Hornet, and while we shouldn't expect double-digit rebounds, Reid is a 3-point option with scoring upside.

Several Memphis Grizzlies: The Ja Morant era has (mercifully) ended. Other than awesome rookie Cameron Boozer (I generally fade first-year players, since someone always jumps too early in drafts), who scores the points? I have doubts about C Zach Edey ever staying healthy, but his ADP reflects said risk. Sophomore SF/SG Cedric Coward is capable of 20 PPG and 8 RPG. PG/SG Scotty Pippen Jr. may average 15 PPG and 7 APG. Even PG/SG Ty Jerome, a popular sleeper but perhaps a bit too coveted in drafts, should deliver solid numbers. Remember, even bad teams produce points, boards and assists.

Others to acquire in the latter rounds: Darius Acuff Jr., PG, Sacramento Kings; Jaime Jaquez Jr., SF/SG, Milwaukee Bucks; Jakob Poeltl, C, Toronto Raptors; Collin Gillespie, PG, Phoenix Suns; Jeremiah Fears, SG/PG, New Orleans Pelicans; Egor Demin, PG/SG, Brooklyn Nets; Cason Wallace, SG/PG, Oklahoma City Thunder; Day'Ron Sharpe, C, Brooklyn Nets.
